exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita: "I wish I'd" curto, com o acento em "wish".
Tell me three things you wish were different now, and two things you wish you had done differently in the past.
exercicios.frase: I wish
exercicios.resposta: I wish I had more time for my children; I work until seven every day. I wish my office were closer to home, and I wish I could speak French. About the past: I wish I'd studied harder at school, and if only I'd bought a house when prices were lower!

exercicios.enunciado: Is it useful to think about our regrets, or is it better to forget them? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: It's useful for a short time, because regrets teach us something. But if you think about them every day, they stop you from living now. Learn the lesson, and then move on.

Describe your childhood: a place, a person, a typical weekend. Use would for at least three repeated actions and used to for at least two states.
exercicios.frase: would
exercicios.resposta: I grew up in Malanje, in a house with a big yard. I used to be very shy, and I used to have a dog called Kito. Every Sunday, my grandfather would take us to the river. We would swim for hours, and he would tell us stories.

exercicios.enunciado: Was childhood better in the past than it is today? Why, or why not?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: In some ways, yes, because we used to play outside all day, and nobody had phones. But today children have more information and better medicine. I'd say it was different, not better.

exercicios.enunciado: What is the real question, according to Lerato?

exercicios.frase: I'd been working at Mopane for seven years.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita: "I'd been" curto.
Tell me the story of a big change in your life or in the life of someone you know. What had been happening before it, how long, and what changed?
exercicios.frase: been
exercicios.resposta: In 2022, my brother had been working as a taxi driver in Luanda for eight years. He'd been saving money for a long time. One day, a friend offered him a shop in Benguela. He'd never run a business, but he took the risk. Now he has two shops.

exercicios.enunciado: Lerato says: "Nobody's ever ready." Do you agree? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: Yes, I agree, because if you wait until you feel ready, you never change anything. You learn most things after you start. But you should still plan — and save some money first.

Think of two decisions or events that changed your life. Say how your life would be different now if they had not happened, and one thing about your character that made you act in a certain way.
exercicios.frase: wouldn't
exercicios.resposta: If I hadn't taken that course in 2020, I wouldn't be working in IT now — I'd probably be a teacher, like my mother. And if I hadn't moved to Luanda, I wouldn't know my wife. If I were more patient, I'd have stayed at my first job longer.

exercicios.enunciado: Do you believe in luck, or do we make our own luck? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: Both, I think, because luck gives you chances, but you have to see them and take them. Mei's mistake was bad luck, but fixing it was her own work.

Tell me about a choice that changed your life. Do you have any regrets?
exercicios.frase: regret
exercicios.resposta: The turning point was in 2019, when I left a bank to study nursing. I weighed up the options for months. My gut feeling said go. I had second thoughts in the first year. But I don't regret it: if I hadn't taken the plunge, I wouldn't love my job today.

exercicios.enunciado: When you make a big decision, do you trust your gut feeling or a list of pros and cons? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: I start with a list, because it helps me see everything. But in the end, I follow my gut feeling. If the list says yes and my stomach says no, I usually wait.

Talk about a real or imagined choice between two options (two jobs, two cities, studying or working): what you would gain and lose, what worries you, what you wish, and what you decide, with a condition.
exercicios.frase: provided that
exercicios.resposta: I have to choose between a master's in Lisbon and a promotion here. In Lisbon, I'd gain a qualification, but I'd lose two years of salary. What worries me is getting stuck here. I've decided: I'll take the promotion, provided that I can study online at the same time.

exercicios.enunciado: Explain this offer in English: "Proposta: Técnico Superior de Informática, Benguela. Início: 1 de Setembro. Salário: 650 000 Kz por mês. Casa paga durante os primeiros seis meses. Período experimental de 90 dias."
exercicios.frase: trial
exercicios.resposta: It's an offer for a senior IT technician job in Benguela, starting on the first of September. The salary is six hundred and fifty thousand kwanzas a month, and they'll pay for housing for the first six months. There's a ninety-day trial period.
exercicios.contexto: Mediação: as condições de uma proposta.

exercicios.resposta: Ten years ago, I left Huambo to study in Luanda. I'd been living with my parents all my life, so it was hard. I used to call my mother every night. If I hadn't moved, I wouldn't have this job. My only regret: I wish I'd visited my grandparents more often.

exercicios.enunciado: A friend asks: "Should I accept a job abroad?" Give two questions they should ask themselves, and one piece of advice.

exercicios.resposta: First, ask yourself: what would you lose, and could you live with that? Second: in five years, would you regret not trying? My advice: talk to someone who has done it, and save some money before you go.
